agents.templateRepoTriggerReviewDesc: Triggered by GitLab / GitHub repository polling; reviews a merge request whenever it changes
agents.templateRepoTriggerReviewFormDesc: After creating, enable the GitLab or GitHub trigger on the Publish page and add the repositories to watch — the Agent wakes only when a merge request actually changes. The review is posted back as a comment on that request using the `glab` / `gh` CLI already signed in on the server, so that login must be in place. Running a CLI also means this template cannot be read-only: comment-only behaviour (never approve, merge, or push) is enforced by the prompt, not by the execution policy. Binding a code source makes it substantially better: the Agent can check callers and tests against the full repository instead of reading the diff alone.

Default access level for auto-created share links. Keep as "Requires login" and manually change to public after reviewing content.
This applies only to shares created afterward. Access is fixed onto each link when published, so changing this won't affect already-published artifacts.
agentDetail.artifactsShareExpiryDaysDesc: Expiry in days for auto-created share links (1–365).

agentDetail.scmIdleHint: Initial sync not started yet, go to SCM source management to trigger sync
agentDetail.scmErrorHint: Sync failed, please check configuration and retry

agentDetail.envVarsEmptyHint: Environment variables injected into the agent process; also referencable in the system prompt.
agentDetail.skillsDesc: Mount skills or collections to extend the agent with focused capabilities.
agentDetail.mcpServersDesc: Connect MCP servers to give the agent external tool access.
agentDetail.kbDocumentsDesc: Mount knowledge base documents as reference material for the agent.
agentDetail.workspaceDesc: The working directory for agent runs — a temp directory or an SCM source.
agentDetail.probeUnsupportedAuthMode: {{provider}} no longer supports the selected credential mode. Pick another mode above, then fetch models again.

agentPublish.successDesc: Your Agent is now available via HTTP API. Copy the endpoint and API key below.
agentPublish.noteDesc: After publishing, the Agent will start running. If it is already running, a new publish will overwrite the current configuration. Please proceed with caution.
agentPublish.keyHiddenPlaceholder: API key exists (hidden for security; click reset to regenerate)
agentPublish.resetKeyConfirmContent: Resetting will invalidate the current API key. Any existing integrations using the old key will stop working. Continue?
agentPublish.ipWhitelistPlaceholder: One IP/CIDR per line, leave empty for no restriction
agentPublish.ipWhitelistHelp: Only allow specified IP addresses to invoke this Agent
agentPublish.apiKeyWarning: Save this key securely. It will not be shown again.
agentPublish.authTypeOauthHelp: Callers authenticate with your enterprise OIDC provider and present the resulting JWT (typically an access token). Access can be opened to all enterprise users or limited to specific ones.
agentPublish.channelsHelp: Select one or more channels to publish the Agent
agentPublish.trustForwardedIdentityDesc: When enabled, upstream agents holding this agent's A2A key may assert their original end-user identity (email), and this agent's runs and audit entries are attributed to it. Enable only if you trust every caller holding the key — possession of the key is equivalent to being able to impersonate any user.
agentPublish.slackChannelDesc: Receive and reply to messages through Slack Socket Mode.
agentPublish.slackSetupIntro: Complete these steps in Slack App Management first. OAuth scopes and event subscriptions are separate settings; missing either one prevents messages from working.
agentPublish.slackStepSocketDesc: Open Settings → Socket Mode, enable Socket Mode, and create an App-Level Token (xapp-...) with connections:write.
agentPublish.slackStepOauthDesc: Open Features → OAuth & Permissions and add the base Bot Token Scopes. files:read receives user files and files:write returns Agent artifacts. After changing scopes, you must Install/Reinstall to Workspace and copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-...).
agentPublish.slackBaseScopes: Base scopes (messages, Slack Files, and artifact delivery)
agentPublish.slackAllMessageScopes: Additional scopes for every channel message
agentPublish.slackEventsRequired: Open Features → Event Subscriptions and add these required events under Subscribe to bot events:
agentPublish.slackEventsOptional: Add these only when “Trigger on every new channel message” is selected:
agentPublish.slackEventWarning: Successful OAuth authorization does not mean message events are subscribed. Without this step, Slack will not deliver messages to a2wave.
agentPublish.slackCredentialsTitle: Enter the Slack credentials in a2wave
agentPublish.slackTriggerOnNewMessage: Trigger on every new channel message
agentPublish.slackTriggerOnNewMessageHint: Also subscribe to message.channels and message.groups, and grant channels:history and groups:history.
agentPublish.slackTestHelp: Add the bot to the test channel, then send @Bot hello; you can also DM the bot. Ordinary channel messages do not trigger when only “Trigger on @mention” is enabled.
agentPublish.slackConfigRequired: App ID, App Token, and Bot Token are required when Slack is enabled.
agentPublish.discordChannelDesc: Receive and reply to messages through the Discord Gateway.
agentPublish.discordSetupHelp: Create a bot, enable Message Content Intent, and invite it with View Channels, Send Messages, Read Message History, and Attach Files. Add Send Messages in Threads when using thread channels.
agentPublish.discordTriggerOnNewMessage: Trigger on every new channel message
agentPublish.discordTriggerOnNewMessageHint: Enable Message Content Intent under Developer Portal → Bot → Privileged Gateway Intents. Only human messages are processed; bot and webhook messages are ignored to prevent loops.
agentPublish.discordConfigRequired: Application ID and Bot Token are required when Discord is enabled.
agentPublish.slackSendArtifactsAsFileHelp: Upload artifacts directly to Slack; requires files:write. When off, only a2wave download links are sent.
agentPublish.discordSendArtifactsAsFileHelp: Upload artifacts directly to Discord; the bot needs Attach Files. When off, only a2wave download links are sent.
agentPublish.nativeDmAlwaysTriggers: Every direct message from a user triggers the Agent.
agentPublish.feishuAppSecretConfiguredPlaceholder: Configured — leave blank to keep, type to replace
agentPublish.feishuTriggerOnNewMessage: Trigger on all new group messages
agentPublish.feishuTopicTriggerOnNewComment: Trigger on new comment in topic
agentPublish.feishuTopicReplyMentionTargetHint: "Mention the trigger sender" and "Mention the topic creator" apply to topic replies only — ordinary group messages always mention the trigger sender. "Do not mention anyone" applies to every group reply. Mentioning the topic creator reads the root message sender; if that lookup fails no one is mentioned, so a triggering bot is not notified by mistake. Supported for plain-text and rich-text replies only.
agentPublish.feishuTopicInjectRootMessage: Include the topic root message content
agentPublish.feishuTopicInjectRootMessageHint: When enabled, topic replies additionally fetch the topic's first message (text/images/files) and inject it into the prompt. Disabled by default: context relies on the session history within the same topic.
agentPublish.feishuCardTemplateIdHelp: The template must be authorized for this App in Feishu Open Platform. Universal template ID: AAqv4DiIGy5jy
agentPublish.feishuCardCreateLink: Open CardKit to create a card
agentPublish.feishuInteractiveCardSetup: "Interactive card": the Agent can send cards with confirm/cancel buttons, text inputs, single/multi selects, and date pickers; the user's input is sent back and resumes the same session.
agentPublish.feishuDebugCardHelp: When checked, append the selected runtime info to the end of each normal reply (handy for troubleshooting); appends nothing if none are checked.
agentPublish.feishuSendArtifactsAsFileHelp: When enabled, artifacts generated by the Agent will be sent as files directly in the Feishu chat
agentPublish.feishuFetchUserInfoHelp:
When enabled, the sender's name and email will be fetched via the Feishu Contact API and placed under `user_info` (cross-channel unified fields: email, name, mobile, source). When disabled, `user_info` is null.
Required scopes (base: contact:contact.base:readonly; field-level: contact:user.base:readonly + contact:user.email:readonly) are already in the permissions list above; make sure the Feishu app has been re-versioned before enabling.
agentPublish.feishuWelcomeHelp: Proactively send an intro of the bot's capabilities + usage guidelines when a user enters the P2P chat with the bot or the bot is added to a group. Markdown supported; delivered as an interactive card.
agentPublish.feishuWelcomeMessagePlaceholder:
👋 Hi, I'm the XX assistant

I can:
- Capability 1
- Capability 2

**Usage guidelines**: …
agentPublish.feishuWelcomeOnP2pEnabledHelp: Decided by the idle threshold below when the user opens the chat with the bot
agentPublish.feishuWelcomeP2pIdleDaysHelp: Re-send when last message is older than this many days; 0 = send every time
agentPublish.feishuWelcomeOnGroupAddedEnabled: Send when bot is added to a group
agentPublish.feishuWelcomeOnGroupAddedEnabledHelp: Fires once on the moment of being added (admins can pin it for long-term visibility)
agentPublish.feishuWelcomeEventsHint: Subscribe to these Feishu events in the Open Platform's Event Subscription panel: im.chat.access_event.bot_p2p_chat_entered_v1 (user enters bot P2P chat) and im.chat.member.bot.added_v1 (bot added to chat). The required im:chat scope is auto-included in the scopes JSON above once welcome is enabled — just submit it and re-version the app.
agentPublish.feishuConfigRequired: Please fill in App ID and App Secret
agentPublish.feishuSetupTitle: How to connect a Feishu bot?
agentPublish.feishuSetupDesc: Pick a way to start. Either way, you'll finish by pasting the App ID / App Secret below.
agentPublish.feishuSetupExisting: I already have a Feishu app
agentPublish.feishuSetupExistingDesc: You've created a custom app on the Feishu Open Platform — just fill in App ID / App Secret.
agentPublish.feishuSetupCreateDesc: Open the Feishu Open Platform to create a new app (bot capability, permissions, long-connection events), then fill in the credentials.
agentPublish.feishuCreateGuideTitle: Create an app on the Feishu Open Platform
agentPublish.feishuCreateGuideStep1: Click the button below to open the Feishu Open Platform and create a custom app.
agentPublish.feishuCreateGuideStep2: Enable the Bot capability; grant the permissions listed below (use "Copy scopes JSON" to import in one go).
agentPublish.feishuCreateGuideStep3: Under Events & Callbacks, choose the Long Connection subscription mode and add the im.message.receive_v1 event.
agentPublish.feishuCreateGuideStep4: Publish a version, then copy the App ID / App Secret from Credentials & Basic Info into the fields below and publish.
agentPublish.a2aServiceDesc: When enabled, other agents can invoke this agent via the A2A protocol.
agentPublish.scheduleCronHelp: Standard 5-field cron: min hour dom mon dow
agentPublish.scheduleCronInvalid: Unsupported Cron expression. Please use one of the supported formats.
agentPublish.scheduleIntentHelp: Message sent to Agent on each trigger. Supports {{date}}, {{time}}, {{iso}} variables
agentPublish.scheduleRunAsOwnerHelp: When on, scheduled runs carry your enterprise SSO identity, for reaching gateway services that require one.
agentPublish.scheduleRunAsOwnerNeedBind: You haven't bound an enterprise identity, so runs can't use your identity.
agentPublish.scheduleCronRequired: Please fill in the cron expression
agentPublish.scheduleIntentRequired: Please fill in the trigger intent (message sent to Agent on each trigger)

agentPublish.chatAppChannelDesc: Generate a shareable chat page link so signed-in colleagues can talk to this Agent directly
agentPublish.chatAppLinkHelp: Share this link with colleagues. Visitors must sign in to a2wave, and every conversation is recorded in run history.
agentPublish.chatAppLinkAfterSave: Save the Agent to get its chat page link.
agentPublish.chatAppDisplayNamePlaceholder: Leave blank to use the Agent name
agentPublish.chatAppWelcomeMessagePlaceholder: Describe what this Agent can do…

agentPublish.chatAppSuggestedQuestionsPlaceholder:
One question per line

agentPublish.chatAppSuggestedQuestionsHelp: One per line, up to {{max}}. Visitors can tap one to ask it directly.
agentPublish.chatAppShowCreatorHelp: Display this Agent's creator in the page sidebar.
agentPublish.chatAppAllowAttachmentsHelp: Uses the global attachment limits (type, size, count).
agentPublish.chatAppShowThinkingHelp: Reveal tool calls and intermediate steps. Turn off for a cleaner, purely conversational view.
agentPublish.chatAppAccessHelp: The chat page is never anonymous: visitors must sign in to a2wave and have read access to this Agent, and every conversation is recorded in run history for auditing.
agentPublish.oauthChannelDesc: Callers authenticate with a JWT issued by your enterprise OIDC provider; open it to everyone or to named members
agentPublish.oauthAccessAllIdaasDesc: Any employee who authenticates through enterprise OIDC can invoke this Agent; the token must carry an email claim or it is denied.
agentPublish.oauthChannelHelpAllIdaas:
Callers authenticate with your enterprise OIDC provider, then send the resulting JWT (typically an access token) in the Authorization header.
Current scope: all enterprise users — anyone who passes OIDC can invoke it.
Note: this channel verifies OIDC-issued JWTs whose aud is on the administrator allowlist; SAML login produces no token usable on this channel.
agentPublish.oauthEnvMissing: Missing enterprise OIDC environment variables; the OAuth channel is unavailable
agentPublish.oauthEnvInvalidPublicKey: The enterprise OIDC config is unusable, so the OAuth channel cannot verify caller tokens.
agentPublish.cardDescApi: Call the Agent over HTTP — for backend services and scripts.
agentPublish.cardDescOauth: Authenticate callers with a JWT issued by your enterprise OIDC provider, no API key to hand out.
agentPublish.cardDescA2a: Expose this Agent to other agents over the A2A protocol.
agentPublish.cardDescFeishu: Chat with the Agent in Feishu, in group chats and DMs.
agentPublish.cardDescSlack: Chat with the Agent in Slack channels and DMs.
agentPublish.cardDescDiscord: Chat with the Agent in Discord servers and DMs.
agentPublish.cardDescSchedule: Trigger the Agent automatically on a cron schedule.
agentPublish.cardDescChatApp: Publish a shareable web chat page for signed-in colleagues.
agentPublish.transportFeishuWsHint: This instance opens the Feishu long connection itself; no public callback URL is needed.
agentPublish.transportSlackSocketModeHint: This instance opens the Slack Socket Mode connection itself; no public callback URL is needed.
agentPublish.transportDiscordGatewayHint: This instance opens the Discord Gateway connection itself; no public callback URL is needed.
agentPublish.connErrorHint: The connection status could not be read; the socket may or may not be up. Check that the service is reachable and retry.
agentPublish.connPendingHint: The switch was changed but not published yet, so the connection is unchanged. Click Publish / Update to apply it.
agentPublish.connScopeHint: Status reflects this server instance only
agentPublish.enableNeedsConfig: Finish configuring this channel before enabling it.
agentPublish.publishOnlySettingHint: Some settings here only take effect after you publish.

agentPublish.oauthAllowedEmailsPlaceholder: Search by name or email, or type an address and press Enter

agentPublish.title: Publish Configuration
agentPublish.oauthRequiresFeishu: Feishu App ID and App Secret are required when the access scope follows Feishu app visibility.
agentPublish.oauthAccessFeishuScopeDesc: Callers must be inside this Feishu app's user visibility scope. App ID and App Secret are required.
agentPublish.oauthChannelHelpFeishuScope:
Callers must authenticate with your enterprise OIDC provider and present the resulting JWT.
The current access scope also checks the Feishu app's user visibility scope.
agentPublish.cardDescGlab: Poll repositories with glab and wake the Agent only when an MR actually changes.
agentPublish.cardDescGh: Poll repositories with gh and wake the Agent only when a PR actually changes.
agentPublish.gitTriggerSetupHelp: The platform reads repository state through the CLI on your chosen interval and triggers the Agent only when an MR/PR really changed. The polling itself costs no tokens — that is the difference from a schedule, which launches the Agent on every tick.
agentPublish.gitTriggerCliUnknown: Not checked yet. Click Check to see whether the CLI is installed and logged in.
agentPublish.gitTriggerCliNotReady: The CLI is not usable yet; polling will keep failing.
agentPublish.gitTriggerCliSelfManaged: The platform only probes — it does not install or log in. Install {{binary}} on the server yourself and run `{{binary}} auth login`.
agentPublish.glabRepoHint: Paste the repository URL. An MR link resolves to its repository.
agentPublish.ghRepoHint: Paste the repository URL. A PR link resolves to its repository.
agentPublish.gitTriggerRepoInvalid: Unrecognised repository URL. Use a full address such as https://host/group/repo.
agentPublish.gitTriggerIntervalHint: {{min}}–{{max}} seconds. Shorter is more responsive but hits the forge more often.
agentPublish.gitTriggerIgnoreDraftsHint: Skip draft / WIP requests so the Agent is not woken too early.
agentPublish.gitTriggerIntentHint: Click a placeholder to insert it. It is replaced with the real MR/PR details at trigger time, so the Agent does not have to look up what changed.
agentPublish.gitTriggerEventRequired: Select at least one trigger event
agentPublish.gitTriggerIntervalInvalid: Poll interval must be between 30 and 600 seconds
agentPublish.oauthEnvIncompleteSettings: The current OIDC channel configuration is incomplete (empty audience allowlist). Complete it in Settings → Enterprise Login; editing environment variables will have no effect.

agentRoute.title: A2A Route
agentRoute.titleDesc: Configure local agents or standards-compliant remote A2A 1.0 / 0.3 services that this agent can invoke.
agentRoute.localAgentsDesc: Select route targets from published A2A agents
agentRoute.localAgentsPlaceholder: Search and select published A2A agents…
agentRoute.remoteAgentsDesc: Add remote A2A services through Agent Card discovery or a direct endpoint
agentRoute.remoteAgentCardHint: Recommended. The card advertises the protocol version, endpoint, and optional capabilities automatically.
agentRoute.remoteDirectStreamingHint: Direct endpoints use blocking SendMessage because no Agent Card is available to advertise streaming support. Live remote child output is unavailable; use Agent Card discovery to enable it when supported.
agentRoute.remoteCallerProvenanceHint: Explicitly send the upstream user's display name and this Agent's name to an a2wave-compatible endpoint. This is audit/display data, not authentication.
agentRoute.remoteDescriptionPlaceholder: Describe the agent's capabilities to aid routing (optional)
agentRoute.remoteApiKeyPlaceholder: Auth token for the remote agent (optional)
agentRoute.showLocalChildOutput: Show local agent output (streaming card mode only)
agentRoute.showRemoteChildOutput: Show remote agent output (streaming card mode only)
agentRoute.noTargetsHint: With no route targets configured, Agent Router lists all published A2A agents without filtering. Adding targets restricts routing to specified agents only.
agentRoute.emptyHint: No route targets configured yet. Remote standards-compliant A2A 1.0 and 0.3 services are supported.

auth.setupDesc: Set admin password to get started
auth.loginDesc: Sign in to continue using A2WAVE
auth.logoutConfirmDesc: Signing out revokes the current session token; you will need to sign in again to continue.

ssoError.GENERIC: SSO sign-in failed. Try again or contact your admin.
ssoError.OAUTH_NOT_CONFIGURED: SSO sign-in is not configured on the server. Contact your admin.
ssoError.OAUTH_DISABLED_BY_ADMIN: Admin has not enabled SSO sign-in yet.
ssoError.SSO_PUBLIC_URL_NOT_SET: The server has no public base URL configured, so a callback URL cannot be generated. Ask your admin to set it under Settings → Artifacts.
ssoError.SSO_DISCOVERY_FAILED: Could not reach the identity provider. Try again later or contact your admin.
ssoError.SSO_FLOW_EXPIRED: The sign-in session expired. Please start again.
ssoError.SSO_FLOW_INVALID: The sign-in request is invalid or already used. Please start again.
ssoError.SSO_TOKEN_EXCHANGE_FAILED: Token exchange with the identity provider failed. Try again or contact your admin.
ssoError.SSO_NOT_IMPLEMENTED: This sign-in method is not available yet. Contact your admin.
ssoError.INVALID_IDAAS_TOKEN: The identity token failed verification. If you just signed in and this keeps happening, it is usually not an expired token but a mismatch between the Issuer / Key ID / IdP public key under Settings → Enterprise Login and what the IdP actually issues (the Issuer must match exactly, trailing slash included). Ask an administrator to check Audit Logs, where the server records the specific reason.
ssoError.IDAAS_TOKEN_MISSING_EMAIL: The identity provider did not return an email. Ask your admin to check the IdP configuration.
ssoError.EMAIL_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED: Your email domain is not on the allow-list. Contact your admin.
ssoError.USER_NOT_PROVISIONED: Auto-provisioning is off. Sign in with password first, or ask admin to add your account.
ssoError.ACCOUNT_DISABLED: Account is disabled. Contact your admin.
ssoError.EMAIL_ALREADY_BOUND: This email belongs to a local password account, so the SSO identity cannot be linked automatically. Sign in with your password and use "User menu → Link enterprise identity", or contact your admin.
ssoError.BIND_REQUIRES_LOGIN: Linking an enterprise identity requires signing in first. Sign in and try again.
ssoError.SHARE_BAD_RETURN: Invalid share address; can't start sign-in. Go back to the original share link and retry.
ssoError.IDAAS_SUB_ALREADY_BOUND: That enterprise identity is already linked to another account and can't be linked again.
ssoError.IDAAS_IDENTITY_ALREADY_BOUND: That enterprise identity is already linked to another account and can't be linked again.
ssoError.SAML_AUDIENCE_MISMATCH: The SAML assertion's Audience does not match this service's SP EntityID. Ask an admin to verify that the callback URL / SP EntityID under Settings → Enterprise Login → SAML matches the IdP registration character for character (localhost and 127.0.0.1 are not interchangeable).
ssoError.SAML_RESPONSE_UNSOLICITED: The SAML assertion does not correspond to this login request (InResponseTo check failed). Start again from the login page; if it keeps failing, ask an admin to confirm the IdP is not using an IdP-initiated flow.
ssoError.SAML_MISSING_IDENTITY: The SAML assertion carries no usable user identifier (NameID). Ask an admin to check the attribute mapping on the IdP side.

kbDocuments.emptyDescription: Add Feishu / Notion documents or upload files to build your knowledge base.

kbDocuments.basicInfoDesc: The name and description will be used to guide the Agent on when and how to reference this document. Write them clearly for best results.
kbDocuments.basicInfoDescCreate: The description guides the Agent on when and how to reference these documents. It is applied to every document added this time.
kbDocuments.feishuPermissionTip: The Feishu app requires these permissions: wiki:wiki or wiki:wiki:readonly for wiki docs; docx:document or docx:document:readonly for docx docs. Apply them in Feishu Open Platform → App Permissions.
kbDocuments.notionConfigDesc: Update the synced page or rotate the Integration Token.
kbDocuments.notionTokenKeepHint: Leave blank to keep the current token.

kbDocuments.filesMaxExceeded: At most {{max}} files at a time — please split it into batches.

memory.title: Long-term Memory
memory.desc: Enable file-based long-term memory for the Agent, persisting context across sessions
memory.enableDesc: When enabled, the Agent can search historical work logs and long-term memory via Skill
memory.recallLevelDesc: Controls how proactively the Agent searches work logs before tasks
memory.recallLevel_weak_tip: Only searches work logs when the user explicitly asks to recall; no proactive search otherwise
memory.recallLevel_medium_tip: Auto-searches work logs for troubleshooting, data queries, architecture decisions and similar experience-driven tasks; skips for simple tasks
memory.recallLevel_strong_tip: Searches work logs before every task to fully leverage past experience
memory.selectFile: Select a file to view its content
memory.deleteConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete "{{filename}}"? This action cannot be undone.
memory.modelDesc: Auto work summaries, scoped insight routing, legacy topicization previews, and log consolidation use the Agent Provider credentials but can run with a lighter model.
memory.modelInheritedDesc: Currently inherits {{model}} from the Agent Provider configuration.
memory.modelOverrideDesc: This model is used only for automatic memory maintenance tasks.
memory.embeddingDesc: Configure an embedding model to enable semantic search (vector/hybrid modes). Without this, only keyword search is available.
memory.embeddingEnableDesc: When disabled, memory search uses keyword matching only
memory.embeddingBaseUrlDesc: Provide an OpenAI Embeddings API compatible endpoint
memory.searchConfigDesc: Post-processing settings for search results, applied to both Agent calls and UI search
memory.decayDesc: Recent history scores higher; curated topics and the MEMORY.md startup catalog are exempt
memory.decayHalfLifeDesc: Logs older than this many days score 50% lower, default 14; 0 disables decay
memory.mmrDesc: Maximal Marginal Relevance — reduces redundancy in search results
memory.mmrLambdaDesc: 0 = maximum diversity, 1 = pure relevance ranking, default 0.7
memory.contextModeDesc: Automatically inject memory content into the system prompt at conversation start
memory.contextMode_off_tip: No memory content is injected automatically. The Agent can search memory on demand via the a2wave-memory skill.
memory.contextMode_memory_tip: Injects the compact MEMORY.md startup summary and topic catalog. Detailed topics and historical logs are disclosed on demand through the a2wave-memory skill.
memory.worklogDesc: Automatically summarize conversations via the Agent Provider after each Run to generate daily work logs
memory.autoInsightDesc: Automatically route durable insights from completed Runs into bounded topics; weak or over-limit candidates remain in Run or worklog history
memory.consolidationDesc: Automatically merge old daily logs into weekly summaries when count exceeds 30, freeing up storage
memory.insightPromptDesc: Available placeholder: {{existingMemory}} (the compact startup catalog, used only to avoid duplicates and choose a stable scope)
memory.topicsDesc: Detailed long-term knowledge is kept in bounded topics and disclosed only when needed.
memory.topicsEmpty: No active topics yet. Automatic insights or an explicit remember request can create one when enough reusable knowledge exists.
memory.sharedAgentWarning: Memory belongs to this Agent and may be shared by all callers who can invoke it. Do not store requester-private secrets or treat it as a personal profile.
memory.legacyDesc: This Agent still uses one unrestricted MEMORY.md. Topicization is a two-step, coverage-checked migration: preview first, then explicitly commit.
memory.topicizeDialogDesc: Every legacy source block must be copied verbatim to exactly one bounded topic. No file changes occur until you confirm.
memory.archivedTopicHint: Archived topic bodies are not disclosed here by default. Reactivate a topic before reading it as active long-term context.
memory.topicSelect: Choose an active topic above to read its complete long-term knowledge here.
